_comment: The real config behind the weather-mode log. Kept as a worked example — copy it, change the stages, point shots_dir at your screenshots. Run: python3 docs/feature-log/build.py docs/feature-log/example.json
title: Portfolio rebuild — visual log
heading: Portfolio rebuild, start to finish
lede: Every screenshot below was rendered in Chromium during the work — real pages, not mockups. Four stages: a correctness pass, a weight cut, a visual refresh, and a live weather mode.

stages.heading: Where it started
stages.note: A working site, but every section was pinned to `96vh`, which forced large empty gaps between them. Four CSS declarations were silently invalid and being discarded by the browser.
shots: Desktop — note the gaps between sections

stages.heading: Correctness and weight
stages.note: No screenshots here, and that is the point — this stage deliberately changed nothing visible. It fixed things that were broken and removed weight nobody was choosing to download.
points: **transition: all 0.3** — no unit, so the whole declaration was dropped. The hamburger menu had never actually animated.
**display: flexbox** — not a real value; the skill layout was silently falling back to block.
**background: (250,250,250)** — missing `rgb()`, so the contact box had no background at all.
**1.1 MB of images referenced by nothing**, and icons shipped at 1000×1000 to be displayed at 32 pixels.

stages.heading: Visual refresh
stages.note: Fixed viewport heights removed, so sections size to their content. Manrope for headings and body, JetBrains Mono for labels and skill tags. One accent, used sparingly. **Page height dropped from 4701px to 3639px with nothing removed.**

stages.heading: Weather mode
stages.note: A cloud button swaps the site into a live sky built from the visitor's real local conditions. Every state below was produced by stubbing the weather API — the only way to photograph snow and lightning from South Florida in August.
callout: **Two bugs found by looking at the output.** A bright midday sky left the near-white page text unreadable, so the sky is now veiled by its own measured luminance — noon gets a heavy scrim, midnight almost none.
And a crisp sun was showing through 97% cloud cover. The disc now fades with real cover and draws after the scrim, since the sun should be the brightest thing in frame.
shots: Clear day — sun placed by real sunrise/sunset
Clear night — stars fade in by sun angle
Rain — angle scales with real wind speed
Snow — flakes sway instead of falling straight
Overcast — 95% cover leaves only diffuse glow
Fog — haze band on the horizon
Reduced motion — same sky, drawn once

footer: Rendered in Chromium at 1440×900 and 390×844 · kanetobey/portfolio-website
